flagged_sentences: On the Cojuangco family’s Hacienda Luisita in Tarlac, a stock-distribution plan approved the next year gave farmworkers shares instead of title to the land.

claims.claim: Hacienda Luisita comprises roughly 4,900 hectares and adopted a stock-distribution plan after 1989 referendums in which workers received 33.296 percent of shares.
claims.episode_span: On the Cojuangco family’s Hacienda Luisita in Tarlac, a stock-distribution plan approved the next year gave farmworkers shares instead of title to the land.
claims.source_title: G.R. No. 171101 - HACIENDA LUISITA, INCORPORATED, PETITIONER, vs. PRESIDENTIAL AGRARIAN REFORM COUNCIL
claims.supporting_quote: Hacienda Luisita, Inc. ... submitted its Stock Distribution Plan ... which was approved by the PARC.

claims.claim: The Presidential Agrarian Reform Council revoked Hacienda Luisita’s stock-distribution plan in 2005; the Supreme Court upheld the revocation in 2011 and 2012.
claims.episode_span: The Presidential Agrarian Reform Council’s 2005 revocation order and the Supreme Court’s 2011 and 2012 rulings confirmed that the stock plan had not transferred effective ownership.

claims.claim: By December 2016 the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program had distributed roughly 4.7 million hectares, yet many large estates remained intact through conversion, dummy holdings, and stock plans.
claims.episode_span: The Ballesteros study for the Philippine Institute for Development Studies found that the overall program had distributed roughly 4.7 million hectares by 2016, yet many large estates remained intact through the very options the 1988 law had permitted.
claims.source_title: The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program After 30 Years: Accomplishments and Forward Options
claims.supporting_quote: CARP land acquisition and distribution accomplishment versus scope, as of December 2016
